close_reason: GOOD observation acknowledged. The 21-test per-sloppy-field sweep (sloppy_field_* in src/lib.rs) is intentional: each test is independently failable, names both the wire field and the typed jscontact target type, and cites a specific RFC 9553 figure as oracle. description:
lib.rs:686-1057 — 21 sloppy_field_* tests, one per Option<serde_json::Value> field on ContactCard, each (1) deserializing hand-written JSON modelled on a specific RFC 9553 figure, (2) further deserializing the inner Value into the corresponding typed jmap-jscontact-types::* type, (3) re-serializing the typed value, (4) asserting back == card.field.unwrap() (i.e., the typed shape round-trips bit-equal to the original Value).

This is the right test pattern for the hybrid Value-with-opt-in-typed design:
- Independent oracle (RFC 9553 figures), per workspace test-integrity rule.
- Each test is small, focused, and asserts a single round-trip — failure points directly at the offending sub-type.
- The sweep covers every sloppy field, not just 'representative ones' — prevents the silent regression where a new field gets added to jmap-jscontact-types but its serde shape diverges from the wire format.
- The test name (sloppy_field_<wire>_roundtrips_through_jscontact_<type>) names both the wire field and the typed shape, making test failure messages self-describing.

A future reviewer will be tempted to consolidate these into a parameterized test or table-driven harness. Don't. Each test is independently failable, independently debuggable, and the per-test rustdoc cites the specific RFC 9553 figure — that traceability is the point.
title: GOOD: per-sloppy-field round-trip test sweep using RFC 9553 figure JSON
